How I got here

I'm a graduate student at the Institute of Education and Research, University of Dhaka, working toward an M.Ed after finishing my B.Ed (Hons). Along the way I spent a term as an intern teacher at a special school for autistic and intellectually disabled children — an experience that shaped how I think about designing for different kinds of learners.

Outside the classroom, I design. I've built branding, social content, infographics, and reports for startups, NGOs, and education platforms — and I currently lead visual content for an education media outlet while researching how tools like memes affect learning in the science classroom.

The common thread is simple: whether I'm writing a lesson plan or laying out a report, I'm trying to make information easier to hold onto.

Graduate Research Project (M.Ed)

Measuring the effect of meme-based instruction on recalling, understanding, and intrinsic motivation of science content among Grade 10 students

An experimental study set inside secondary school science teaching, built to test whether meme-based instruction changes how well students recall and understand content — and whether it moves their intrinsic motivation to learn.

Collected and analysed quantitative data across the three outcomes to identify how meme-based instruction influenced student learning.
